 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnish Bhatnagar
 Order
% 19.10.2023 Crl.M.A. 28834/2023 (exemption)
Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.408/2016, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:26:10 3.

The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 26.06.2012 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.

Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living Surjeet Singh & Ors vs State (Gnct) And Anr on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182038941/
1 separately since 05.10.2014.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 24.06.2016, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

4. Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 21.05.2019 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13B(2) of the HMA was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 29.01.2021 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Courts, Tis Hazari, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, Tis Hazari, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioners no.2 and 3 are not appearing today as they are not well.
He further submits that petitioner nos. 2 and 3 be exempted from appearance.

So,
petitioner nos. 2 and 3 are exempted from appearance in Court today.
6. Petitioner nos. 1 and 4 appear through video-conferencing and Respondent no.2 is present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:26:10 1,00,000/- (bearing no. 021320 drawn on Axis Bank Ltd.) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.408/2016,
under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

However, the rights of the children born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains majority as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh vs.
Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors, decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos.4031-4032 of 2019.
8. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J OCTOBER 19, 2023/
